Rising prices can erode purchasing power, meaning that even if nominal household incomes increase, consumers may not be able to afford more goods and services if their real income remains stagnant or decreases.

National income is not always greater than GDP because GDP measures the total value of all goods and services produced within a country, while national income accounts for income earned by residents, which can be impacted by factors like depreciation and net income from abroad.

exchange rates, local purchasing power, and economic conditions. In this analysis, Mexico

The Federal Reserve can use bond purchases as a policy tool to address an economic
recession by increasing the money supply in the economy. When the Fed buys bonds, it pays
for them with newly created money, which banks receive. This action lowers interest rates,
making borrowing cheaper for consumers and businesses. As a result, lower interest rates
encourage spending and investment, which can help stimulate economic growth. Overall, bond
purchases can lead to increased economic activity, helping to pull the economy out of a
recession.
answers.explanation: correct because it accurately describes how bond purchases by the Federal Reserve increase the money supply, lower interest rates, and stimulate spending and investment, thereby helping to counteract an economic recession.
